title: U.S. House · California's 4th District
area: Covers part of California's North Bay and wine country region, including St. Helena, following the 2025 Proposition 50 mid-decade redistricting.

context.text: The district's boundaries changed as a result of California Proposition 50, approved by voters on November 4, 2025, which redrew the state's congressional map.

Because California uses a top-two primary regardless of party, both general-election candidates are Democrats: Mike Thompson placed first in the June 2, 2026 primary with 41.0% (84,753 votes) and Eric Jones placed second with 22.2% (45,992 votes), ahead of several Republican candidates, out of 206,887 total votes cast.

candidates.name: Mike Thompson
candidates.ballotNote: Placed first in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2023, prior district); member, House Ways and Means Committee

summary.text: Mike Thompson was born and raised in St. Helena, California, enlisted in the U.S. Army and served in combat in the Vietnam War, and later worked at a winery before entering politics. He served in the California State Senate and has represented the North Bay in the U.S. House since 1999, and serves on the Ways and Means Committee. His official biography describes his legislative focus as lowering costs for families, gun violence prevention, clean energy and health care.

background.text: Born and raised in St. Helena, California, in a working-class family; his official biography says he is the grandson of Italian immigrants. Ballotpedia gives his birth year as 1951.

According to his official biography, he dropped out of high school to enlist in the U.S. Army, served in combat in the Vietnam War as a staff sergeant and platoon leader with the 173rd Airborne Brigade, and was wounded in action and awarded the Purple Heart. He later trained others as an instructor at the Army's Airborne School.

After returning home he worked as a maintenance supervisor at Beringer Winery, then used the GI Bill to become the first in his family to earn a college degree, attending Napa Valley Community College and graduating from California State University, Chico; he later earned a master's degree in public administration there. Ballotpedia lists the degrees as 1982 and 1996.
Ballotpedia says he previously worked as a professor and winery owner; his official biography describes him as a small vineyard owner.
Served in the California State Senate from 1990 to 1998, representing the 2nd District and chairing the Budget Committee; his office says he was the first Vietnam veteran elected to the state Senate.
Elected to the U.S. House in 1998 and took office in January 1999, first representing the 1st District and now the 4th District.
In Congress he serves on the Ways and Means Committee, where he is Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Tax and a senior member of the Health Subcommittee.

Was appointed chair of the House Gun Violence Prevention Task Force after the Newtown, Connecticut, school shooting; co-founded and co-chairs the bipartisan Congressional Wine Caucus, co-chairs the bipartisan Military Veterans Caucus, and is a member of the Blue Dog Coalition. He received the Sierra Club's Edgar Wayburn Award.
According to his official biography, he is married to Janet Thompson, a family nurse practitioner, and they have two sons and three granddaughters.

priorities.text: Campaign website cites fiscal responsibility as a priority, calling for a balanced approach to the federal debt that includes spending cuts and higher taxes on those who can afford them, while protecting Social Security and Medicare.
priorities.quote: It is important that we act in a fiscally responsible way while protecting programs like Social Security and Medicare, supporting job creation and also tackling our national debt.

positions.summary: Says addressing the federal debt requires a balanced approach that includes asking higher earners to pay their fair share.
positions.quote: the best way to do this is through a balanced approach that cuts spending, asks everyone to pay their fair share, and creates jobs.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Ways and Means, including its Health and Tax subcommittees, for the 2025-2026 session.
Chaired the Ways and Means Subcommittee on Select Revenue Measures during the 2021-2022 session.

candidates.name: Eric Jones
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, in which both top finishers were Democrats

summary.text: Eric Jones is a Democrat and former venture capitalist, described by the Associated Press as 35 years old, who has not previously held public office. He was a partner at Dragoneer Investment Group before founding a family foundation with his wife and co-founding the American Dream Institute. He is challenging fellow Democrat Rep. Mike Thompson after finishing second in the June 2026 top-two primary.

background.text: Obtained a bachelor's degree from Yale University, according to Ballotpedia.
Worked as a partner at Dragoneer Investment Group; the Associated Press describes him as a former venture capitalist.

After leaving the firm, he and his wife founded the Rachel and Eric Jones Foundation, which describes itself as 'a community-rooted family foundation focused on creating lasting impact across Northern California.'

Co-founded the American Dream Institute, which describes itself as 'a digital engagement engine built by and for the next generation of voices...founded to raise the voices of young Americans from the ground-up.'

Finished second in the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, advancing to a general election against Thompson that the Associated Press described as a generational contest between two Democrats. This is his first run for office.

priorities.text: Campaign centers on an 'Affordability Agenda,' proposing a $10,000 middle-class tax credit, holding PG&E accountable for rate increases, lowering prescription drug prices, and expanding Medicare and universal childcare.
priorities.quote: For too many families, the basics of life feel out of reach. Groceries, housing, utilities, health care — everything keeps getting more expensive while wages stay the same.

positions.summary: Campaign platform calls for universal childcare alongside expanded mental health access.
positions.quote: Eric will fight for universal childcare and expanded access to affordable mental health services so families can work.

positions.summary: Supports expanding Medicare to cover dental, vision, hearing aids, and in-home nursing care.
positions.quote: Eric supports expanding Medicare to cover dental, vision, hearing aids, and in-home nursing care.

positions.summary: Proposes a $10,000 middle-class tax credit as direct relief for working families, funded as part of a broader affordability agenda.

sources.title: Veteran California US House member Mike Thompson will face Democratic challenger in November

researchNotes: Both general-election candidates are Democrats because of California's top-two primary system. Neither has completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; their stated priorities and positions come from campaign-website text reproduced on their Ballotpedia pages. Jones has held no prior public office. Biography gaps: Thompson's official biography gives no years for his Army service or state Senate tenure (Ballotpedia and Wikipedia differ on service dates, so they are omitted); no campaign biography page for Eric Jones was loaded, so his birthplace, upbringing and residence are not documented.
